# Cue calibration

Cohort: 400 synthetic patients from the fitted population prior; calibration on the 50 with unaided accuracy 0.45-0.75 (mean 0.58), 1000 trials each. Target rescue shares from Nardo et al. 2017 (initial phoneme, final phoneme, whole word); semantic is an ASSUMPTION.

| cue | activation level | target rescue share | achieved | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| phonemic_initial | 75 | 0.700 | 0.700 | fitted |
| phonemic_final | 60 | 0.475 | 0.243 | target unreachable: the best the mechanism can do is 0.24 at level 60 |
| whole_word | 25 | 0.825 | 0.822 | fitted |
| semantic | 10 | 0.350 (assumed) | 0.258 | set by assumption to one semantic jolt |

A rescue share is the fraction of items the patient would have failed that are named with the cue. The final-phoneme cue is the informative failure: in the model's six-word neighbourhood the two formal competitors share the target's coda, so a coda cue raises them as much as the target and its benefit peaks low and then reverses. Real final-phoneme cues (Nardo: 0.79 against 0.60 unaided) do better than that, which says real formal competitors share less of the word's ending than the model's do, or that a final sound carries information the model's three-slot phonology cannot represent.

**Prediction 1: cue effect by severity** (not fitted). Pease & Goodglass 1978: phonemic cues named 49% of failed pictures, and responsiveness was lower in more severe patients.

| unaided accuracy band | n | mean unaided | initial-phoneme rescue | semantic rescue | whole-word rescue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| severe, unaided < 0.30 | 40 | 0.21 | 0.46 | 0.11 | 0.67 |
| 0.30-0.50 | 40 | 0.41 | 0.61 | 0.19 | 0.78 |
| 0.50-0.70 | 40 | 0.60 | 0.71 | 0.26 | 0.83 |
| mild, >= 0.70 | 40 | 0.79 | 0.79 | 0.31 | 0.86 |

**Prediction 2: semantic cue by lesion type** (not fitted). Python et al. 2021: semantic cues were ineffective for lexical-semantic anomia and phonological cues worked regardless of profile.

| lesion type | n | mean unaided | semantic rescue | initial-phoneme rescue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| semantic lesion (p/s > 1.3) | 36 | 0.51 | 0.42 | 0.79 |
| balanced | 40 | 0.54 | 0.30 | 0.71 |
| phonological lesion (p/s < 1/1.3) | 40 | 0.52 | 0.15 | 0.61 |

How to read a disagreement here: these two tables are what the SP model, with cues as external activation, says about cases it was not tuned on. Where they match the literature the mechanism is doing work; where they do not, the mechanism is wrong in a stated way.
